title: Variation in the composition of nutrients in the blood of vertebrate hosts affect gonotrophic cycle velocity and the reproductive output of Culex pipiens
content:
Abstract
Deep understanding of vector biology is essential for improving disease control strategies. Most female mosquitoes are anautogenous, requiring a blood meal from vertebrate host for egg development. However, the impact of host blood nutritional composition such as red and white blood cell counts, hemoglobin percentage, total protein, and free amino acids on the gonotrophic cycle remains unclear. In this study, female Culex pipiens were allowed to feed on 4 vertebrate hosts (pigeon, chicken, mice, and human), and the nutritional profiles of the blood meals were quantified. Results revealed that avian blood meals contained higher levels of free amino acids compared to mammalian blood. Females fed on avian hosts exhibited a significantly shorter gonotrophic cycle and enhanced ovarian development. These findings suggest that variation in blood nutritional composition may influence reproductive timing in Cx. pipiens and could contribute to host-associated differences in feeding preference.
